title: What are Native Modules?
overview: Native Modules allow React Native applications to access platform-specific features written in native languages like Java, Kotlin, Objective-C, and Swift. They help connect JavaScript code with native device capabilities.

example.title: Native Module Examples
example.content:
Native features:
• Camera access
• Bluetooth
• Sensors
• File system
• Custom Android/iOS APIs

title: Why Use Native Modules?
overview: Native Modules are used when React Native does not provide a built-in solution for a specific device feature or when native code provides better performance.

example.title: Use Cases
example.content:
Examples:
• Using device hardware
• Integrating native SDKs
• Improving performance-heavy operations

title: Native Module Architecture
overview: Native Modules create communication between JavaScript and native code through React Native's native bridge. JavaScript sends requests to native modules, and native code returns results back.

example.title: Communication Flow
example.content:
JavaScript Code
      ↓
React Native Bridge
      ↓
Native Android/iOS Code
      ↓
Response Back to JavaScript

title: Creating Custom Native Modules
overview: React Native allows developers to create custom native modules when existing libraries do not provide the required functionality. These modules contain native platform code exposed to JavaScript.

example.title: Custom Module Example
example.content:
Android:
• Java/Kotlin Module

iOS:
• Objective-C/Swift Module

title: Using Native Device Features
overview: Many React Native libraries internally use native modules to provide access to device features such as camera, location, notifications, and storage.

example.title: Native Feature Examples
example.content:
Libraries using native modules:
• Camera libraries
• Maps
• Push Notifications
• Bluetooth libraries

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned what native modules are, why they are needed, how JavaScript communicates with native code, and how custom native functionality can be added to React Native applications.

example.title: Quick Revision
example.content:

✔ Used for device-specific features.
